questions.q: In Azure Cost Analysis, what does switching the Granularity control between daily and monthly buckets actually change?
options: Which Azure subscription the report is scoped to
Whether a spike shows up clearly versus only a slow drift being visible
Whether tags can be used as a grouping option at all
Whether the forecast line is shown on the chart
questions.explain: Granularity controls the size of the time buckets the chart is drawn in — daily buckets reveal a sudden spike, while monthly buckets smooth that out and reveal a slower drift instead.

questions.q: Which of these is a grouping option available in AWS Cost Explorer, according to this lesson?
options: Terraform module name
Azure management group
Linked Account, for an AWS Organization with multiple member accounts
Kubernetes namespace
questions.explain: Cost Explorer's grouping dimensions include Service, Linked Account, Region, and Cost Allocation Tag — Linked Account rolls up spend by AWS Organizations member account.

questions.q: What does this lesson say must happen before a tag can be used as a grouping dimension in AWS Cost Explorer?
options: The tag must be removed from all but one resource
The AWS account must be upgraded to an Enterprise support plan
The resource carrying the tag must be in the us-east-1 region
The tag must be explicitly activated as a Cost Allocation Tag in the Billing console
questions.explain: Applying a tag to a resource isn't enough on its own — an administrator has to activate it as a Cost Allocation Tag in Billing before Cost Explorer can group or filter by it.

questions.q: What is the lesson's caution about the forecast line in both Azure Cost Analysis and AWS Cost Explorer?
options: It only works if every resource is tagged with a cost center
It is a trend-based projection — directional, not a guarantee, and slow to react to a newly deployed workload
It automatically applies a budget cap once the forecast exceeds a threshold
It is only available in AWS Cost Explorer, not in Azure Cost Analysis
questions.explain: Both tools' forecasts project the current trend forward, which is useful for spotting a likely overrun early but isn't a guarantee and reacts slowly to brand-new spend.

questions.q: In the lesson's two-step example of investigating whether a feature rollout raised the bill, what is the correct order of operations?
options: Group broadly by service first, then filter narrowly by that feature's tag to confirm where the increase actually lives
Delete the resource first, then check whether the forecast line changed afterward
Filter by tag first, then disable Cost Allocation Tags before grouping
Contact the cloud provider's billing support team before opening either report
questions.explain: The pattern is to group broadly by service to spot where spend moved, then add a tag filter to confirm the increase sits inside the expected team's or feature's resources.
